# Rosara (01, engineer) — SPD-057

## Brief
Build the SPD-057 auto-claim: in a `claim` project (BadTakes), an unclaimed session whose prompt names one of that project's tickets becomes Spud without Eric typing /spud.

Why: three BadTakes sessions started "Work on BAD-006" and one "Start on BAD-020", none with /spud. Each stayed plain: the app titled it from the first message, the session ritual never ran (no `BAD-nnn - <what>` title), and the work happened outside the ledger. `spud ticket show SPD-057` has the full ticket brief; this brief is what you build.

1. A `UserPromptSubmit` hook in bin/spud_ledger.py, written by `spud settings sync` (home) and `spud project install|sync` (a project's untracked .claude/settings.local.json) next to the existing hooks, with the same conventions: a project's hook line carries `--project <key>`, records and fails open (spooling any gap into a `hook.error` event), never blocks a prompt.
2. It acts only when session_mode is `plain` (an unclaimed session in a `claim` project other than the home) and the prompt names the key of a ticket that exists in that session's project. Then it claims the session through the same code path as `spud --as spud session claim` (factor it; do not duplicate the INSERT), records the claim event with how it was claimed (the hook) and the key that triggered it, and returns `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` that makes the session Spud: the /spud skill's steps (read the home's CLAUDE.md and spud.config.json in full, the precedence rule, run the session ritual from step 2, including setting the session title to `<KEY> - <what this session does>`), built from the same source as the installed SKILL.md so the two cannot drift, plus the claim card. Keep it within the harness's inline context limit (see SPD-048 and fit_bytes / CLAIM_CARD_CAP).
3. Matching: word-bounded, the project's own ticket prefix, the ledger's key shape (prefix, dash, exactly the configured pad of digits, three today), and only keys present in the tickets table. Never claim on: the older tracker's numbers BadTakes PRs and TODO.md cite (BAD-23 to BAD-36, two digits), another project's key, a declined ticket, a prompt in the home, an already-claimed session, a caller with an agent_id, a session Eric released with `session release` (a release must stick for that session; add what the schema needs to know that, with a migration if it needs one, following the existing migration pattern and backup), a prompt that is a slash command's expansion of /spud (already claiming). A done ticket does claim (Eric may be reopening it). Case: match the prefix case-sensitively unless the existing key parsing is case-insensitive; follow the code.
4. A `plain` session whose prompt names no ticket stays silent, as today. Nothing changes for `always` projects or the home.
5. Tests in tests/ for every case above (including two-digit old-tracker numbers, `BAD-0060` and `XBAD-006` not matching, release sticking, settings sync and project install/sync writing the hook line, the additional context carrying the ritual and title step), following the existing test style and fixtures. Then the full suite: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (about six minutes; run it in the background and wait), green, with the count in your result.
6. Do not edit CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, or anything under ledger/ or reports/. In your result, include the paragraph CLAUDE.md's "In another project" section and Ledger v1's hooks bullet should gain, for Spud to apply after landing, and whether `spud settings sync` and `spud project sync --all` must be run after the merge.

Work in the current working directory (the SPD-057 worktree, branch worktree-spd-057-auto-claim). Do not commit; Spud commits.
